en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hammam reported to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa ibn Qays, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "The tent is a pearl whose height into the sky is sixty miles; in each corner of it the believer has a family whom the others do not see."

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i narrated to me: Abu 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "In Paradise there is a tent of a single hollowed pearl, its width being sixty miles; in each corner of it are wives whom the others do not see, and the believer visits them in turn."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Abu Qudamah—namely al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd—from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qays, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Indeed, the believer in Paradise has a tent made of a single hollowed pearl, its length being sixty miles; the believer has wives in it whom he visits in turn, and none of them sees the others."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's—they said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us, saying: Ath-Thawri said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me that al-Agharr narrated to him from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "A caller will call out: 'Indeed, it is for you to be healthy and never fall ill, ever; and it is for you to live and never die, ever; and it is for you to be youthful and never grow old, ever; and it is for you to enjoy bliss and never experience misery, ever.' That is His words, Mighty and Majestic: {'And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do"'}."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Whoever enters Paradise will enjoy bliss and never experience misery; his garments will never wear out, and his youth will never perish."

Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me: My father narrated to me: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr reported to me, from Jabir, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, similar to it, except that he said: "and they will be inspired with glorification and magnification just as they are inspired with breathing."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir both narrated to me from Abu 'Asim—Hasan said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us—from Ibn Jurayj: Abu az-Zubayr reported to me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The people of Paradise will eat and drink therein, but they will neither defecate, nor blow their noses, nor urinate; rather, their food will be [expelled through] a burp like the fragrance of musk. They will be inspired with glorification and praise just as they are inspired with breathing." He said: And in the hadith of Hajjaj: "that food of theirs."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash with this chain of narration up to his words: "like the fragrance of musk."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is 'Uthman's; 'Uthman said: narrated to us, while Ishaq said: Jarir reported to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Indeed, the people of Paradise eat and drink therein, but they do not spit, nor urinate, nor defecate, nor blow their noses." They asked: "Then what happens to the food?" He said: "A burp and a sweat like the fragrance of musk; they are inspired with glorification and praise just as they are inspired with breathing."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him—and he mentioned hadiths, among which: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The first group to enter Paradise will have their forms like the form of the moon on the night of the full moon. They will not spit therein, nor blow their noses, nor defecate therein. Their vessels and combs will be of gold and silver, their incense burners of aloeswood, and their sweat musk. Each one of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins can be seen through the flesh because of their beauty. There will be no discord among them, nor any mutual hatred; their hearts will be as one single heart, glorifying Allah morning and evening."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The first group from my nation to enter Paradise will be in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon, then those who follow them will be like the brightest shining star in the sky, then after that they will have different ranks. They will not defecate, nor urinate, nor blow their noses, nor spit. Their combs will be gold, their incense burners aloeswood, and their sweat musk. Their disposition will be upon the character of a single man, on the height of their father Adam: sixty cubits." Ibn Abi Shaybah said: "upon the character of a man," while Abu Kurayb said: "upon the physical stature of a man." And Ibn Abi Shaybah said: "upon the form of their father."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa': Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The first to enter Paradise..."; (and a different chain) Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Qutaybah's—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise will be in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be like the brightest radiant star in the sky. They will not urinate, nor defecate, nor blow their noses, nor spit. Their combs will be gold, their sweat musk, their incense burners aloeswood, and their spouses the wide-eyed houris. Their disposition will be upon the character of a single man, in the form of their father Adam: sixty cubits tall into the sky."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: Men and women disputed as to which of them would be more numerous in Paradise, so they asked Abu Hurayrah, and he said: Abu al-Qasim, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said—the like of the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah.

'Amr an-Naqid and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ad-Dawraqi both narrated to me from Ibn 'Ulayyah—and the wording is Ya'qub's—they said: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Ayyub reported to us, from Muhammad, who said: Whether they were boasting or discussing whether men or women will be more numerous in Paradise, Abu Hurayrah said: Did not Abu al-Qasim, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise will be in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon, and the one that follows it will be like the brightest radiant star in the sky; each man among them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins will be seen through the flesh, and there will be no bachelor in Paradise"?

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Basri narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a marketplace to which they will come every Friday. Then a north wind will blow and scatter fragrance upon their faces and their garments, and they will increase in beauty and grace. They will return to their families having increased in beauty and grace, and their families will say to them: 'By Allah, you have increased in beauty and grace after us!' And they will say: 'And you, by Allah, have increased in beauty and grace after us!'"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Among those of my nation who love me most intensely will be people coming after me, each of whom would wish he could see me even at the cost of his family and his wealth."

'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to me: Ma'n narrated to us: Malik narrated to us; (and a different chain) Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me—and the wording is his: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas reported to me, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise will look up at the occupants of the high chambers above them just as you look at a brilliant distant star on the horizon from the east or the west, because of the superiority that exists between them." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, are those the dwellings of the prophets, which no one else can reach?" He said: "Yes, by the One in Whose hand is my soul! They are people who believed in Allah and affirmed the truth of the messengers."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Al-Makhzumi reported to us: Wuheyb narrated to us, from Abu Hazim with both chains of narration, similar to the hadith of Ya'qub.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise will look up at the chambers in Paradise just as you look at the stars in the sky." He said: I narrated that to an-Nu'man ibn Abi 'Ayyash, and he said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: "just as you look at a brilliant star on the eastern or western horizon."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sahm narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas reported to us; (and a different chain) Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me—and the wording is his: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah will say to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They will say: 'Here we are, our Lord, at Your service, and all good is in Your hands.' He will say: 'Are you well-pleased?' They will say: 'Why should we not be well-pleased, O Lord, when You have given us what You have not given to anyone else among Your creation?' He will say: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They will say: 'O Lord, what thing could be better than that?' He will say: 'I bestow My pleasure upon you, so I will never be angry with you after it, ever.'"

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali narrated to us: Al-Makhzumi reported to us: Wuheyb narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without traversing it." Abu Hazim said: I narrated it to an-Nu'man ibn Abi 'Ayyash az-Zuraqi, and he said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated to me from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider of a well-trained, swift thoroughbred horse travels for a hundred years without traversing it."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, and he added: "without traversing it."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that he said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years."

Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli both narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Sakhr narrated to me that Abu Hazim narrated to him, saying: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd as-Sa'idi say: I attended a gathering with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in which he described Paradise until he concluded, then he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said at the end of his hadith: "In it is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of any human being." Then he recited this verse: {"Their sides part from their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend of what We have provided them. And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes as a reward for what they used to do"}.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his: My father narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of any human being'—as a treasured store, not to mention that which Allah has disclosed to you." Then he recited: {"And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes"}.

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of any human being—as a treasured store, not to mention that which Allah has disclosed to you.'"

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—Zuhayr said: narrated to us, while Sa'id said: Sufyan reported to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of any human being.'" The confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah: {"And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes as a reward for what they used to do"}.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to me, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit and Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir reported to us, from Mansur; (and a different chain) Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is his: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Shaqiq Abu Wa'il, who said: 'Abdullah used to remind us every Thursday, so a man said to him: "O Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman, we love your discourse and yearn for it, and we would love for you to speak to us every day." He said: "Nothing prevents me from speaking to you except that I dislike causing you boredom. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to space out the days when admonishing us, out of fear that weariness might overtake us."
